evidenceAudit.scope: Average-risk adults: when to start colorectal cancer screening in Saudi Arabia, which test and interval, follow-up of positive tests, and when symptoms need referral instead. Verified against the Saudi PHA Clinical Preventive Guideline 2023 (start at 45 locally), the USPSTF 2021 recommendation and NICE NG12 (symptomatic FIT pathway).
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: Higher-risk (family history, Lynch) surveillance intervals not reproduced
Saudi FIT positivity thresholds by laboratory not checked

pathophysiology.summary: Most colorectal cancers develop from adenomatous polyps over about 10 years. Screening finds cancers early and removes polyps. Colorectal cancer is the most common cancer in Saudi men and third in Saudi women (SOS 2014).
keyMechanisms: Adenoma–carcinoma sequence gives time for detection and polypectomy.
Faecal immunochemical test (FIT) detects human haemoglobin from bleeding lesions.
A positive stool test needs colonoscopy to find the source.

symptoms: Symptoms (rectal bleeding, change in bowel habit, iron-deficiency anaemia, weight loss) need the symptomatic pathway.
physicalSigns: Abdominal and rectal examination if symptomatic; pallor.
redFlags: Iron-deficiency anaemia — FIT and referral pathway (NICE NG12 1.3.1)
FIT 10 µg Hb/g or more in a symptomatic adult — suspected cancer referral (NICE 1.3.2)

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Bright red bleeding; still assess risk.

ruleIn.testName: Faecal immunochemical test (FIT) or guaiac FOBT
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: All positive non-colonoscopy tests need timely colonoscopy (PHA).

clinicalManagement.title: Who
actions: Saudi PHA: start at 45 (based on American Cancer Society); USPSTF: 45–49 (B) and 50–75 (A).

clinicalManagement.title: Positive test
actions: Arrange timely colonoscopy after any positive non-colonoscopy test (PHA).

clinicalManagement.title: Symptoms
actions: Do not use screening for symptoms: offer FIT per NICE NG12 1.3.1; refer if 10 µg Hb/g or more, rectal mass, or strong concern.

learningObjectives: Screen average-risk adults for colorectal cancer from 45.

keyPoints: FIT yearly or colonoscopy every 10 years.
Symptoms → NICE FIT pathway, not screening.
pitfalls: Screening FIT in a patient with rectal bleeding and weight loss.
No colonoscopy after a positive FIT.

patientEducation: Screening can prevent cancer by removing polyps.
lifestyleAndDiet: Physical activity, healthy weight, less red and processed meat, stop smoking.
mdtReferrals: Endoscopy for positive tests; genetics for suspected Lynch syndrome.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Repeat at the interval for the chosen test (PHA).
